title: Leviathan
globalRules: The central apparent threat is benign; never invent a hostile monster to reward a player theory.
The coronal mass ejection and station failures remain objective threats.
Messages escalate according to the source sequence, with timing controlled by real-time, paced or accelerating mode.
Station problems may be ignored; consequences continue without forcing repair.
The central AI can be damaged or destroyed if the fiction/rules permit it.
Player theories are tracked as beliefs, never truth flags.

clocks.note: Exact source message count/order must be replaced with PDF-verified values.
Represents intensifying coronal mass ejection/environmental danger.
Degrades when source station problems are ignored or worsen.

scenes.title: Wake Without Memory
requiredFacts: The characters wake on a space station without memories.
Something is wrong with the station and nearby star.
hiddenFacts: The apparent central creature/threat is benign.

choices.label: Check the central computer for logs or identity data
Check station alarms and system status
Look outside and inspect the star
Inspect your equipment and immediate surroundings
Explore the station manually

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Route any plausible investigation to station systems/features without adding a hostile creature or fabricated backstory.

scenes.title: The Central Computer
requiredFacts: The central AI is a major information/malfunction channel.

choices.label: Ask who you are and why you are here
Ask what emergency is in progress
Diagnose the AI for errors
Disconnect or disable the AI

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Allow interrogation, hacking, repair or violence according to chosen ruleset. The AI is not protected from consequences.

choices.label: Prioritise the most urgent station failure
Ignore repairs and keep investigating
Ask the AI to explain or assist
Inspect the star and exterior systems

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Players set priorities. Unaddressed source problems remain active and generate their natural consequences.

scenes.title: Something Is Happening to the Star
requiredFacts: The nearby star is producing an intensifying coronal mass ejection.
hiddenFacts: The frightening interpretation of the messages/phenomenon is not a literal hostile monster.

choices.label: Measure the stellar event
Prepare the station against the solar event
Compare what you see with the cryptic messages
Move away from the viewports and inspect the station

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Give real environmental observations only. Do not validate hallucinated creatures through description.

scenes.title: Who Were We?
requiredFacts: Characters have amnesia but may inspect possessions, bodies and surroundings for clues.

choices.label: Search clothing and equipment for identity clues
Check for signs explaining the memory loss
Compare what you find with station records

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Use source identity/amnesia clues once PDF-verified. Do not invent a human-experiment conspiracy.

scenes.title: Search the Station
requiredFacts: The station contains clues and increasingly disruptive problems.

choices.label: Follow the strongest clue you've found
Inspect the airlock and pressure systems
Inspect the sleep/cryogenic pods
Inspect external power/solar systems
Return to the central computer

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Use the PDF map/key once available. Until then, only verified functional station areas may be treated as canon.

scenes.title: Keep the Station Together
requiredFacts: A station problem can be fixed, failed or ignored.

choices.label: Attempt a proper repair
Make a temporary workaround
Leave it and focus elsewhere
Use the AI or station automation to assist

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Use selected ruleset only when failure has meaningful consequences. Routine competent work may simply succeed.

scenes.title: The AI Is Not Helping
requiredFacts: AI malfunctions become part of the escalating scenario.

choices.label: Try to diagnose or repair the AI
Ignore the AI and work manually
Shut the AI down
Let the AI continue and look for useful information

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: AI behaviour uses source malfunction table once verified. Do not make every malfunction actively malicious.

scenes.title: Silence the Machine
requiredFacts: Players can damage/destroy the central AI.

choices.label: Continue using manual station systems
Try to recover logs/data from the damaged system
Wait and see whether the feared threat arrives

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Do not resurrect the AI simply to deliver exposition. Continue only through surviving source-consistent channels.

scenes.title: What Do You Think Is Happening?
requiredFacts: Players are expected to form competing theories from incomplete evidence.
hiddenFacts: The central apparent threat is benign.

choices.label: Act as if something hostile is approaching
Search for evidence of an experiment or manipulation
Treat the AI as the main threat
Assume the stellar event is the real danger and focus on survival

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Record theory as player belief and let actions follow. Never promote theory to truth without source evidence.

scenes.title: Wait for the Thing That Might Not Exist
requiredFacts: Players may bunker down rather than continue exploration.
hiddenFacts: No invented attack should occur merely to punish waiting.

choices.label: Stay hidden and wait
Use a sleep/cryogenic pod as shelter
Fortify against a possible breach
Resume investigating before conditions worsen

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Advance paced/accelerating clocks and natural station consequences. Do not spawn a fake attacker.

scenes.title: Another Message
requiredFacts: The next source message/event advances mystery and pressure.
hiddenFacts: The final sequence leads to the benign reveal.

choices.label: Follow the new clue
Prioritise worsening station systems
Challenge the AI about the message
Hold position and wait for the next development

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Insert exact PDF-verified message/problem beat at runtime. When source final-message/reveal condition is reached, transition to reveal.

scenes.title: What Leviathan Really Was
requiredFacts: The source's final information reveals that the central feared threat is benign.

choices.label: Focus on surviving the remaining stellar danger
Stabilise the station after the panic
Work out which clues you misunderstood
Leave the station if an escape option remains

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: The reveal ends the paranoia mystery but does not erase objective damage from the coronal mass ejection or ignored station failures.

endings.title: The Monster Was in the Explanation
endings.summary: The characters reach the benign truth behind the apparent central threat and understand how ambiguous evidence and fear shaped their interpretation. Remaining station damage is resolved separately.

endings.title: Survive the Station
endings.summary: The characters survive or escape the stellar/station crisis after the core mystery resolves, with consequences determined by the systems they repaired, ignored or destroyed.

endings.title: Too Much Left Broken
endings.summary: Objective station/environment failures become fatal or force abandonment even though the feared central creature was never the real threat.

endings.title: Waiting for an Attack
endings.summary: The characters spend critical time defending against a threat that does not arrive while station/solar conditions continue to worsen; eventual outcome depends on remaining integrity and source final message.
